title: I'm a composer and sound designer. I made a game to teach myself FMOD. It became a first-person adaptation of Clark Ashton Smith's 'The Empire of the Necromancers' - Here is a Pre-Alpha Demo
author: burgric
selftext:
An early-development video game adaptation of Clark Ashton Smith's macabre tale of two necromancers who seize the throne of a dead city and resurrect its long-departed inhabitants to serve their diabolic ends.

As the Lich — one of the many dead resurrected as the sorcerers swept through a desert necropolis — you must discover your own identity and that of the necromancers as you journey to Yethlyreom, city of your forebears, to put an end to their designs.

I started this project about 9 months ago to teach myself FMOD. I wanted to apply what I was learning, so started working with Claude to build a game set in Clark Ashton Smith's Zothique setting, learning Unity and FMOD as I went.

The writing, voice work and music are my own (FL Studio/EastWest instrument libraries). All SFX are human made, either recorded by myself or sourced royalty-free and then edited/mixed by hand in Audacity and FMOD. The final title card was created with After Effects.

Meshy/Gemini provided a significant amount of 3D/2D assets which were heavily curated and edited throughout the process. I also used many human-made assets. Every AI-assisted asset was built using carefully-crafted prompts inspired by the literary and artistic works of Smith and the stories of Arabian Nights, which deeply influenced him. The necropolis design, its monuments and characters' appearances were inspired by that influence, as well as the culture of the Abbasid Empire and the Greco-Roman world.

Smith was a member of the Lovecraft circle and a major contributor to the magazine Weird Tales in the 1930s, along with Robert E. Howard of Conan the Barbarian fame. Although he considered himself primarily a poet, he is also remembered for his decadent stories set in strange, otherworldly places, such as Zothique, the last inhabited continent on Earth in the far flung future, where sorcery and demonism prevail again as in ancient days.

While composing, I tried many styles, textures and instrumentation choices before landing on the current soundtrack, which is a hybrid of traditional Arabic instrumentation and maqamat, Middle-Eastern percussion and dungeon synth elements.

YouTube keeps defaulting to 360p when loading the video. I recommend switching to 1080p as OBS was a bloody pain to get a decent recording with. If anyone knows of more user-friendly screen capture software, feel free to recommend.
